events.title: Wrong Platform
events.body: A parent slides a sealed copy of Goblin Kart for NovaCube across the counter. "My kid's birthday is tomorrow and I just realized — they have the PrismBox, not whatever this is. Please tell me there's something we can do."

choices.label: Swap it for the PrismBox copy at the same price.

result.headline: Exchange Accepted
result.acknowledgement: Exchange logged. The customer relaxes at the counter.
result.customer_reaction: The parent exhales hard, then gives you a tired, grateful nod.
result.store_outcome: You swap the sealed copy for the right platform, keep the sale, and move the line along without drama.
result.manager_note: Vic would rather eat a clean exchange than lose a customer over a box that never got opened.

consequences.label: Money
consequences.text: +$15 sale kept at the register.

consequences.label: Reputation
consequences.text: +2 satisfaction from a clean fix.

consequences.label: Inventory
consequences.text: Correct PrismBox copy leaves the shelf; sealed NovaCube copy moves to the back room.

consequences.label: Policy
consequences.text: +2 manager trust for honoring the exchange without drama.

choices.label: Bundle the PrismBox copy with a discounted used controller.

result.headline: Bundle Sold
result.acknowledgement: Bundle logged. The customer accepts the extra item.
result.customer_reaction: The parent hesitates at the extra total, then caves when you point out the used controller discount.
result.store_outcome: The register lands a bigger sale, but the exchange feels a little less like help and a little more like pressure.
result.manager_note: Good numbers, softer trust. Vic notices both.

consequences.label: Money
consequences.text: +$18 from the bundle sale.

consequences.label: Reputation
consequences.text: +1 satisfaction, tempered by the pressured upsell.

consequences.label: Inventory
consequences.text: Correct PrismBox copy and discounted used controller leave the store; sealed NovaCube copy moves to the back room.

consequences.label: Policy
consequences.text: No manager-trust change; the sale is allowed, but it reads pushy.

choices.label: Point at the "opened or sealed, no exchanges" sign and decline.

result.headline: Exchange Refused
result.acknowledgement: No sale logged. The customer gathers the box to leave.
result.customer_reaction: The parent goes quiet, gathers the game, and leaves with the receipt crushed in one hand.
result.store_outcome: The register stays unchanged, but the next customer in line watches the whole thing happen.
result.manager_note: Policy protected the drawer. It did not protect the room.
result.hidden_hint: At the door, the parent turns back like they almost want to say something else, then thinks better of it.

consequences.label: Money
consequences.text: $0 because no exchange or sale happens.

consequences.label: Reputation
consequences.text: -3 satisfaction after the public refusal.

consequences.label: Inventory
consequences.text: No inventory changes; the customer leaves with the wrong-platform copy.

consequences.label: Policy
consequences.text: -2 manager trust and a visible customer-risk note for the hardline call.

events.title: The Scratched Disc
events.body: A regular slides a stack of disc cases across the counter. "Trading these in — same deal as last time. Except this one." He taps a case on top. "I know it's scratched. I'm hoping you'll still count it full value since I've been coming here for years."

choices.label: Count it full trade-in value — he's a regular.

result.headline: Full Value Accepted
result.acknowledgement: Trade-in logged. The regular leaves with full credit.
result.customer_reaction: The regular looks relieved that you honored the relationship.
result.store_outcome: You take the scratched disc into the damaged bin and keep the rest of the trade-in moving.
result.manager_note: Vic can live with a small hit when it keeps a repeat customer steady.

consequences.label: Money
consequences.text: -$8 in extra trade-in value.

consequences.label: Reputation
consequences.text: +3 from backing a regular.

consequences.label: Inventory
consequences.text: Two clean trade-ins move to the back room; the scratched disc goes to damaged stock.

consequences.label: Policy
consequences.text: +1 manager trust for keeping the exception controlled.

choices.label: Offer half value on the scratched disc, full on the rest.

result.headline: Partial Value Offered
result.acknowledgement: Trade-in logged. The regular accepts the split valuation.
result.customer_reaction: He grumbles, then nods when you separate the clean cases from the scratched one.
result.store_outcome: The store gets the good stock and keeps the damaged disc from being priced like shelf-ready inventory.
result.manager_note: That is the kind of middle lane Vic wants: fair, clear, and documented.

consequences.label: Money
consequences.text: $0 net after balancing the trade-in credit.

consequences.label: Reputation
consequences.text: +1 for treating the regular fairly.

consequences.label: Inventory
consequences.text: Two clean trade-ins move to the back room; the scratched disc is tracked separately.

consequences.label: Policy
consequences.text: +2 manager trust for valuing condition honestly.

choices.label: Decline the scratched disc per policy, process the rest.

result.headline: Scratched Disc Declined
result.acknowledgement: Trade-in logged. The regular keeps the damaged disc.
result.customer_reaction: He is annoyed, but he still lets you process the clean cases.
result.store_outcome: You protect the damaged-bin standard and add the usable trade-ins to back-room stock.
result.manager_note: Vic will take the cleaner books, even if the conversation cooled off.

consequences.label: Money
consequences.text: +$4 after declining the damaged disc.

consequences.label: Reputation
consequences.text: -2 from a disappointed regular.

consequences.label: Inventory
consequences.text: Only the clean trade-ins move into store inventory.

consequences.label: Policy
consequences.text: +1 manager trust for holding the damaged-stock line.
